items.title: Compliance with the Order dated 12.06.2026 of the Hon’ble Revisional Authority regarding re-examination of the issues raised w.r.t the application of M/s Agrow Allied ventures Private Limited for grant of registration for indigenous manufacture of Fluxametamide Technical 93.5 % min. u/s 9(3) TIM vs TI of the Insecticides Act, 1968.
items.decision: RC perused the Order dated 12.06.2026 passed by the Hon'ble Revisional Authority whereas the matter had been remanded by the Hon'ble Minutes of 473rd RC meeting held on 29.06.2026 Revisional Authority for a limited review of the issues relating to the manufacturing process, impurity profile and any potential toxicological implications arising therefrom. RC also perused the letter dated 22.06.2026 from M/s Godrej Agrovet ltd. The Committee was apprised that, in compliance with the directions of the Hon'ble Revisional Authority, the complete chemistry dossier and all documents available on record were re-examined. The Committee noted that the applicant had submitted the requisite documents prescribed under the extant TIM vs. TI Guidelines, including the list of raw materials and intermediates with source of supply, stepwise manufacturing process, chemical equations, flow sheet diagram from raw materials to the final technical product, effluent treatment method, specifications, method of analysis, impurity profile and supporting analytical data. The Committee further noted that chemical equivalence had already been established with the registered source, M/s Godrej Agrovet Limited, and that the chemical composition, specifications and impurity limits submitted by the applicant were identical to those of the registered source. The Committee also noted that an in-process sample drawn during inspection by officers of the Directorate had been tested by the Central Insecticides Laboratory (CIL) and found to conform to the submitted specifications. The CIL analysis did not reveal any unidentified impurity or any additional impurity having any toxicological concern. The reported impurity profile was within the prescribed limits and no toxicologically significant impurity arising from the disclosed manufacturing process was detected. The Committee further deliberated upon the concerns raised before the Hon'ble Revisional Authority regarding the manufacturing process and the possible formation of toxicologically significant impurities. After examining the chemistry dossier, impurity profile, CIL analytical report and other material available on record, the Committee observed that no chemistry-related deficiency or safety concern has been established. The available data do not indicate the formation or presence of any additional toxicologically significant impurity under the disclosed manufacturing process. Minutes of 473rd RC meeting held on 29.06.2026 The RC also noted that the petitioner's contention regarding the use of chloroform during the manufacturing process, including the alleged possibility of the formation of isocyanides and it’s derivatives or any other additional impurities arising therefrom, is not revealed from the technical dossier or the reports available on record. The Committee observed that no such concerns are reflected in the technical documentation or analytical reports submitted by the applicant or generated by the Central Insecticides Laboratory. Accordingly, the RC found no merit or substance in the averments made by the petitioner in this regard. Accordingly, the Registration Committee, after thorough re-examination of the matter in compliance with the Order dated 12.06.2026 of the Hon'ble Revisional Authority and considering the available material on records, found no reason to interfere with its earlier decision taken in the 470th RC Meeting under Agenda Item No. 6.54, to grant registration for the indigenous manufacture of Fluxametamide Technical 93.5% Min. under Section 9(3) of the Insecticides Act, 1968, in the TIM vs. TI category, to M/s Agrow Allied Ventures Private Limited. The Committee, therefore, decided to uphold its earlier decision for grant of registration for indigenous manufacture of Fluxametamide Technical 93.5% Min. under Section 9(3) (TIM vs TI) to M/s Agrow Allied Ventures Private Limited, with a provisional shelf life of two years based on Accelerated Storage Stability (ASS) data, in accordance with the decision of the 424th RC (Agenda Item No. 10.48). The applicant shall submit real- time shelf-life data within two and a half years from the date of submission of the application, failing which the Registration Certificate shall be deemed cancelled. The existing condition shall continue to form part of the Certificate of Registration. RC directs the Secretary, CIB&RC to communicate this decision to the Hon’ble Revisional Authority and the respective Parties.

items.title: Judgement dated 29.05.2026 passed by the Hon’ble Delhi High Court in LPA No 215/2023, Dhanuka Agritech Limited v/s Union of India & Ors. Minutes of 473rd RC meeting held on 29.06.2026
items.decision: RC perused the Judgement dated 29.05.2026 passed by Division Bench of the Hon’ble Delhi High Court in the above matter and observed that the impugned decisions of the RC taken in its 430th meeting and as amended in 431st meeting granting registration for the import of Halosulfuron Methyl Technical 98% min. and Halosulfuron Methyl 75% WG formulation to M/s Crystal Crop Protection Limited, has been quashed/ set aside. RC also observes that in compliance with the said judgement conveyed by the Union Counsel, the Secretariat of CIB&RC had already written a communication dated 11.06.2026 to M/s Crystal Crop Protection Limited to surrender the original captioned CRs forthwith to the Secretariat of CIB&RC and shall not utilize the same for any purposes whatsoever. The copy of said communication dated 11.06.2026 had also been sent to the respective State Director of Agriculture for taking further appropriate steps in accordance with law. RC also perused an email communication dated 17.06.2026 from M/s Crystal Crop Protection Limited wherein they have informed that they have approached the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India by special leave petition (SLP) challenging the judgement dated 29.05.2026 wherein Union of India and CIB&RC are also arrayed as a party respondent. They have thus assured that they shall not act upon and utilize the above CRs and had requested for a reasonable time to surrender the captioned original certificates pending the initial hearing of the SLP. RC deliberated the issues and is of the considered view that since the decision of the RC taken in its 430th and 431st meeting has been set aside by the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi vide its judgement dated 29.05.2026 and therefore, the same is required to be complied in its true letter and spirit. RC is also of the view that all consequential approvals/ permissions granted by the State Governments also does not survive. RC thus decided that the applicant may be directed to immediately and forthwith surrender the original CRs for the above products to the Secretariat of CIB&RC without any fail. RC also directs the Secretariat of CIB&RC to issue an appropriate communication to the respective State Governments to revoke the manufacturing licenses granted for the captioned CRs and/ or any other action required to be taken in this regard in accordance with law. Further, it was reiterated that the above decision of the RC shall be subject to any of the directions that may be passed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the Special Leave Petition filed by M/s Crystal Crop Protection Limited. RC also directs the Secretary, CIB&RC to take all necessary steps to appropriately deal with the matter including seeking of any inputs/assistance required from the concerned technical experts who had dealt with the matter.

items.decision: The RC deliberated the agenda and re-iterated its earlier decision regarding of import of CRMs in its 470th meeting vide agenda item No. 10.29. It added the following: 1. It may be noted that Certified Reference Materials (CRMs) which may include banned and/or restricted pesticides are analytical standards used exclusively for testing, calibration, method validation, quality control, and standardization purposes in laboratories. These materials are imported Minutes of 473rd RC meeting held on 29.06.2026 and utilized in very small quantities and are not intended for commercial use, formulation, manufacturing, sale, distribution, or field application. Considering their limited quantity and specialized use in analytical and research activities, the Central Insecticides Board & Registration Committee (CIB&RC) has exempted the import of Certified Reference Materials (CRMs) from the requirement of obtaining import permission under the provisions administered by CIB&RC. Stakeholders may therefore import CRMs intended solely for research and development purposes, laboratory testing, calibration, validation, and standardization activities to be carried out in Research and development Laboratories/Centers, testing and calibration laboratories, etc. for testing of pesticides, without obtaining prior import permission from CIB&RC. Keeping this in view, importers are advised to maintain adequate records demonstrating that the imported materials are Certified Reference Materials and are being used exclusively for the aforesaid purposes. For the import of chemicals and laboratory reagents which are included in the schedule of the Insecticides Act, 1968, the RC has directed Secretary, CIB&RC to arrange for a joint meeting with DCPC, DGFT, Customs and FSSAI to gauge the situation, and discuss present issues. The proceedings and minutes of the meeting and any decisions thereof shall be presented to the RC for further consideration and review.

items.title: Clarification is required for the scrutiny of Insecticidal paint formulation application submitted by M/s. Indigo Paints Limited for the registration of Permethrin 1 % SC insecticidal Paint formulations in compliance with the decision of 449th RC meeting. The Registration Committee observed that the applicant has sought registration of Permethrin 1% in Paint under the Household category.
items.decision: The Committee noted that products of this nature appropriately fall under the Biocide category. RC deliberated the agenda in detail and observed that the guidelines for biocides have been stayed by the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi and the matter is under sub-judice. The Committee further noted that, two similar applications for insecticidal paint had been considered and those applicants had furnished additional data to facilitate comprehensive human health and environmental risk assessment. Accordingly, in view of the regulatory precedent and without prejudice to the outcome of the matter pending before the Hon'ble High Court, the present application may also be considered under the Household category, subject to submission of the following information, as furnished by the earlier applicants: 1. Ecotoxicity studies based on the proposed use pattern. Minutes of 473rd RC meeting held on 29.06.2026 2. Complete chemical composition of the paint formulation under affidavit, along with Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS)/Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for each component and supporting scientific literature. 3. A declaration certifying that no component of the formulation is known to cause carcinogenicity, teratogenicity (developmental toxicity), reproductive toxicity or other chronic adverse health effects at the proposed use concentration. 4. Details of the global use pattern, registration status and approved label claims for insecticidal paints containing the proposed active ingredient. 5. Data on air concentration of the insecticide in the vicinity of the painted surface at different time intervals following application. 6. Available information on human health and environmental safety from countries where such insecticidal paints are in use. 7. Proposed use pattern in India along with the proposed strategy for public awareness and communication in the event of registration. The application shall be placed before the Registration Committee for further consideration only after submission and satisfactory evaluation of the above information.
